# Review of FDS Section 6.2, Tank Pressure Control

I used only the text you gave. There is no instrument index, cause-and-effect chart, alarm database or SRS, so I wrote those items out in the corrected section. Values marked "confirm" are my proposals.

## 1. Defect list

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-01 | 6.2.1 | The control mechanism is missing. "Controls capacity" does not say how (speed, unloading, suction throttle, recycle). The PV transmitter tags, output, action, mode behavior and redundancy are also missing. | Define PV (PT-501A/B/C, median), output, action and mode behavior (FR-BOG-001 to 005). |
| D-02 | 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3, 6.2.6 | Setpoints are written in prose. This breaks the single source of truth. | Move all values to the setpoint list. Use IDs in the text. |
| D-03 | 6.2.1 | There is no duty/standby logic for K-501A/B, and no start or stop sequence. | Add the state table, start/stop sequences and standby start (FR-BOG-006 to 012). |
| D-04 | 6.2.2 | PIC-510 is not tied to PIC-501. The text gives no reset hysteresis, no PV-512 fail position and no PT independence. It does not say what happens if the flare is unavailable. | Define PIC-510 as a separate controller with its own deadband. Set the fail position. Add a flare-unavailable alarm (FR-BOG-013 to 016). |
| D-05 | 6.2.3 | Tripping the BOG compressors on tank high-high pressure is a hazard. It removes the main means of lowering tank pressure at the moment it is needed. "To protect them" is not a valid reason, because tank pressure is not a compressor limit. | Remove the trip. Compressors stay at maximum load. Compressor trips come from machine protection only (FR-BOG-017). |
| D-06 | 6.2.3 | The text does not say whether high-high is BPCS or SIS. A tank overpressure function that is credited as a safety layer belongs in the SRS (IEC 61511). | Reference the SRS function. The BPCS only annunciates (FR-BOG-018). |
| D-07 | 6.2.4 | An HMI bypass of a high-high trip is not acceptable. It has no authority control, time limit or alarm, and no MOC or bypass procedure. | Delete it. If a maintenance override is needed, it applies to the BPCS machine trip only. It needs a key switch and a time limit, and it raises an alarm (FR-BOG-019). The SRS governs any SIS bypass. |
| D-08 | 6.2.5 | The statement "low pressure is not a concern" is wrong. Compressors that control on pressure can still pull the tank to vacuum. This can happen on sensor failure, a stuck-open recycle, or a falling BOG rate during low ambient heat ingress or after unloading. | Add a low-pressure limiter, a low-low stop and a make-up requirement (FR-BOG-020 to 023). |
| D-09 | 6.2.5 | "Run continuously" conflicts with duty/standby, trips, minimum load and restart. It cannot be tested. | Define the running state, its exits, and restart after trip or power loss. |
| D-10 | 6.2.6 | Relief set pressures are in prose. They are not a control function. The text does not show a setpoint ordering check. The low-side protection has no stage between normal and the vacuum relief. | Reference the relief datasheets. Put the values in the list. Add the ordering check and the low-low stop. |
| D-11 | 6.2.7 | Anti-surge is deferred to the vendor. The narrative states no required behavior, no interaction with PIC-501 and no fail position. The compressor type is not stated. | State the required behavior (FR-BOG-024 to 026). Confirm the compressor type (OI-01). |
| D-12 | Whole section | Bad PV, comms loss, power loss and restart are missing. So are alarms, operator interface and open items. No requirement has an ID or a test. | Add the sections below. |
| D-13 | 6.2.2 and 6.2.3 | The tag naming is inconsistent. High-high has no tag, and PIC-510 has no PT. | Assign PT-501A/B/C, PT-510 and PAHH-501 (confirm against the instrument index). |

## 3. Corrected section

### 6.2 Tank Pressure Control

**6.2.1 Purpose and boundaries**
This section covers pressure control of tank T-501 with BOG compressors K-501A/B and flare control valve PV-512. It does not cover the tank overpressure and vacuum protection functions in the SRS. It does not cover the relief valves, which the relief datasheets define.

**6.2.2 Equipment and tags (confirm against the instrument index)**

| Tag | Function |
|---|---|
| PT-501A/B/C | Tank pressure. Median is the PV for PIC-501. |
| PT-510 | Tank pressure, independent tap. PV for PIC-510. |
| PIC-501 | BOG compressor capacity controller |
| PIC-510 | Flare control valve controller |
| PV-512 | Tank vapor to flare valve. Fail position closed (confirm, OI-02). |
| K-501A/B | BOG compressors |
| PAHH-501 | High-high pressure. Action per SRS. |

**6.2.3 States and transitions (each K-501 unit)**

| State | Entry permissives | Exits | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stopped | Stop sequence complete, or trip reset | Starting | Operator | Operator-prompted |
| Starting | All start permissives true (see FR-BOG-007) | Running, or Tripped | Operator, or auto (standby) | Automatic |
| Running | Start sequence step 4 done | Stopping, or Tripped | PIC-501 | Automatic |
| Stopping | Operator stop, or PALL stop | Stopped | Operator, or auto | Automatic |
| Tripped | Any trip in 6.2.6 | Stopped | Operator reset | Manual |

Operations sign-off is required for these states and for the prompts in 6.2.8.

**6.2.4 Requirements**

| ID | Requirement | Test (FAT) |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BOG-001 | PIC-501 uses the median of the good PT-501A/B/C as PV. | Simulate PT values. Check the median. |
| FR-BOG-002 | PIC-501 is direct acting. Capacity increases as PV rises above SP-01. | Step PV. Check output direction. |
| FR-BOG-003 | PIC-501 output sets the load of the running K-501 units. | Check the load command at 0%, 50%, 100%. |
| FR-BOG-004 | In manual, the operator sets the capacity. The low-pressure limiter and all trips stay active. | Set manual. Lower PV below SP-07. Check the limit. |
| FR-BOG-005 | PIC-501 tracks the actual load when the vendor package is in local control. | Put the package in local. Check tracking and bumpless return. |
| FR-BOG-006 | The operator selects K-501A or K-501B as lead. The other unit is standby. | Select each lead. Check the roles. |
| FR-BOG-007 | Start permissives: PV above SP-10, no active trip on the unit, vendor package ready, PIC-501 not in fault. | Remove each permissive. Check the start is blocked. |
| FR-BOG-008 | Run the start sequence in 6.2.5 on an operator START command. | Run the sequence. |
| FR-BOG-009 | Start the standby unit when the lead unit trips. | Trip the lead unit. Check the standby start. |
| FR-BOG-010 | Start the standby unit when PV stays above SP-12 for SP-13 and the lead unit is at maximum load. | Hold PV above SP-12. Check the start after the delay. |
| FR-BOG-011 | After a stop from PALL or power loss, do not start any unit automatically. Prompt the operator. | Cycle power. Check there is no auto start. |
| FR-BOG-012 | Run the stop sequence in 6.2.5 on an operator STOP command. | Run the sequence. |
| FR-BOG-013 | PIC-510 uses PT-510 as PV. Its output is zero while PV is below SP-02. | Ramp PT-510. Check the output at SP-02. |
| FR-BOG-014 | PV-512 closes when PV falls below SP-02 minus SP-11. | Ramp down. Check the close point. |
| FR-BOG-015 | If PT-510 is bad, PIC-510 uses the PT-501 median. | Fail PT-510. Check the transfer and the alarm. |
| FR-BOG-016 | PV-512 moves to its fail position on loss of air or signal. | Remove air. Check the position. |
| FR-BOG-017 | Do not trip K-501 on tank high pressure. Trip K-501 only for the causes in 6.2.6. | Raise PV to SP-03. Check that K-501 keeps running. |
| FR-BOG-018 | PAHH-501 raises an alarm in the BPCS. The protective action is in the SRS. | Raise PV to SP-03. Check the alarm. |
| FR-BOG-019 | The BPCS has no HMI bypass of any trip in 6.2.6. A key-switch maintenance override of the machine trip (CE-02) is allowed for SP-17 at most. It raises an alarm. | Operate the override. Check the alarm and the expiry. |
| FR-BOG-020 | When PV is below SP-07, the low-pressure limiter reduces the PIC-501 output to the minimum load. | Lower PV. Check the limit. |
| FR-BOG-021 | When the median PV is below SP-08 for SP-09, stop all running K-501 units. | Lower PV. Check the stop and the latch. |
| FR-BOG-022 | A PALL stop is latched. Reset needs PV above SP-10 and an operator action. | Try to reset below SP-10. Check it is refused. |
| FR-BOG-023 | Pressure make-up for low tank pressure is handled per OI-03. | See OI-03. |
| FR-BOG-024 | The anti-surge system keeps each K-501 above its minimum flow in all states. | Vendor FAT test |
| FR-BOG-025 | The anti-surge valve opens on a trip and on loss of signal. | Trip and fail the signal. Check the position. |
| FR-BOG-026 | PIC-501 requests the load. The anti-surge controller has priority over PIC-501. | Request low load. Check that the anti-surge recycle stays active. |

**6.2.5 Sequences**

*Start sequence (SqBC), each K-501 unit*

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Check start permissives | All true | TM-01 | Abort. Alarm. Unit stays Stopped. |
| 2 | Start vendor auxiliaries | Auxiliaries ready | TM-02 | Stop auxiliaries. Alarm. Stopped. |
| 3 | Start the driver | Driver at speed | TM-03 | Stop the driver. Trip. Start the standby. |
| 4 | Load the unit under PIC-501 | Unit loaded | TM-04 | Unload. Trip. Start the standby. |

*Stop sequence*

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Unload the unit | Minimum load | TM-05 | Go to step 2 and alarm. |
| 2 | Stop the driver | Driver stopped | TM-03 | Trip. Alarm. |
| 3 | Stop auxiliaries | Auxiliaries stopped | TM-02 | Alarm. |

**6.2.6 Interlocks (cause and effect)**

| ID | Cause | Effect | Latched or auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CE-01 | Median PV below SP-08 for SP-09 | Stop all running K-501 | Latched | Operator reset with PV above SP-10 |
| CE-02 | K-501 machine protection trip (vendor list) | Trip that unit. Start the standby. | Latched | Operator reset at the HMI after the cause clears |
| CE-03 | Start sequence step timeout | Trip that unit | Latched | Operator reset |
| CE-04 | PT-501 deviation, two or more bad | PIC-501 output goes to SP-16. The operator is prompted to take manual. | Auto-reset | Auto, when two PTs are good |
| CE-05 | PAHH-501 | Alarm only in the BPCS | Auto-reset | Auto. SIS reset per SRS. |

SIS actions for tank overpressure and vacuum are in the SRS.

**6.2.7 Alarms (no alarm database was given)**

| Tag | Condition | Priority (confirm) | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|
| PAH-501 | PV above SP-06 | Medium | Check the K-501 load and the standby. Start the standby. |
| PAHH-501 | PV above SP-03 | High | Check the SIS action. Check PV-512 is open. |
| PAL-501 | PV below SP-07 | Medium | Check the limiter and the make-up. |
| PALL-501 | PV below SP-08 | High | Check that K-501 stopped. Do not restart until PV is above SP-10. |
| PDA-501 | PT deviation above SP-14 for SP-15 | Low | Check the PT. |
| K-501 TRIP | Any trip in 6.2.6 | High | Check the cause. Reset. Check the standby. |
| PV-512 OPEN | PV-512 open | Medium | Check the BOG load and the flare. |
| FLARE UNAVAIL | Flare system not ready (flare interface, OI-04) | High | Reduce BOG input. Call the supervisor. |
| COMMS K-501 | Vendor comms lost for TM-06 | Medium | See 6.2.8. |

**6.2.8 Abnormal handling**

| Event | Response |
|---|---|
| One PT bad | Use the median of the other two. Alarm. |
| Two PT-501 bad | CE-04. PIC-501 output to SP-16. |
| PT-510 bad | See FR-BOG-015. |
| PT-510 and PT-501 median both bad | PIC-510 holds the last output. Alarm. The operator takes manual. |
| Vendor comms loss | The package holds the last load. PIC-501 shows bad status. The operator goes to local control if the loss continues. |
| Power loss | K-501 stops. PV-512 goes to its fail position. |
| Power restart | No auto start (FR-BOG-011). The operator starts the lead unit when permissives are true. |
| Air loss | PV-512 goes to its fail position. The anti-surge valve opens (FR-BOG-025). |

**6.2.9 Operator interface**
The operator sees PV (PT-501 median and PT-510), the setpoints, the PIC-501 and PIC-510 outputs, the K-501A/B state, the lead selection and PV-512 position. The operator changes PIC-501 mode, SP-01, the lead selection and the START/STOP commands. The operator is prompted to start after a power restart, to reset after a trip, and to take manual after two bad PTs. Operations sign-off is required for the prompts.

**6.2.10 Open items**

| ID | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Confirm the compressor type and capacity control method | Integrator | 2026-11-15 |
| OI-02 | Confirm the PV-512 fail position by HAZOP | Process safety | 2026-11-30 |
| OI-03 | Define the make-up source for low tank pressure (valve, tag, setpoint) | Process lead | 2026-11-30 |
| OI-04 | Define the flare interface signal | Process lead | 2026-11-15 |
| OI-05 | Confirm the tags against the instrument index | Controls lead | 2026-11-15 |
| OI-06 | Confirm all "confirm" values in the setpoint list | Process and operations | 2026-11-30 |
| OI-07 | Align with the SRS: PAHH-501 action and the vacuum protection function | Safety lead | 2026-11-30 |
| OI-08 | Get the vendor list of K-501 machine protection trips for CE-02 | Integrator | 2026-11-15 |

The STE pass is done on the requirement and sequence text. The sentences are within the length limits.
